candidate.educational_objective: Reduce environmental trip hazards as part of fall prevention.

options.A: Keep pathways to the bathroom and door clear of clutter, cords, and unnecessary equipment.
options.B: Store equipment in the walking path so it is easy for staff to reach.
options.C: Leave loose electrical cords across the route to the bathroom.
options.D: Dim the room and place personal items where the client must climb to reach them.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ fall-prevention guidance recommends a safe environment with clear, unobstructed pathways and removal of clutter and cords that can create trip hazards.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Clear pathways free of clutter and cords reduce environmental fall hazards.
candidate.source_document_title: The Falls Management Program—Ways Families Can Help Reduce Fall Risk
candidate.source_locator: Reduce clutter—keep pathways clear; remove cords, furniture, and other items from walking areas
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
candidate.stem: Which environmental action best supports fall prevention in a hospitalized client’s room?
